newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Golkar heads for sweeping victory.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Golkar heads for sweeping victory.

text.p: Indonesia's ruling Golkar party headed for a landslide general election victory on Friday, taking 74.42 percent of the votes counted by 7 a.m. (0000 GMT).
The Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) also pushed up its share of the votes, while the big loser was the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), badly split in a bitter leadership battle.
Election officials said at 7 a.m. that of the 80 million votes counted, Golkar had won nearly 60 million, or 74.42 percent. This was about 2.5 million votes short of an unassailable majority.
Nearly 125 million voters were eligible to cast their ballots in Thursday's poll but the turnout was not immediately known.
The PPP had won 18.25 million votes, or 22.78 percent, while the PDI trailed far behind with 2.2 million votes, or 2.80 percent.
In the last elections in 1992, Golkar won 68 percent of the vote, PPP 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.
A foreign analyst closely monitoring the election said he expected Golkar's final vote to come slightly above its declared target of 70.02 percent, with the PPP the big winner in percentage terms.
"However, nobody expected the PDI vote to collapse like this," he said.
Analysts said spoiled ballots and abstentions as a form of protest would help push up Golkar's final share of the vote.

Figures released shortly before 8 a.m. (0100 GMT) gave Golkar 63,751,579 votes of the 86,296,132 votes counted. Nearly 125 million people had been eligible to cast their ballots, but the number who actually voted was not immediately known.
The PPP was also a big gainer in percentage terms, with 20,102,765 vote or 23.30 percent. The PDI lagged far behind with 2,441,788 votes, or 2.83 percent.
In the last elections in 1992, Golkar took 68 percent of the vote, the PPP 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.
"It seems that Golkar will have its heart's wish, it will probably have a landslide," analyst Dewi Foruna Anwar of the Centre for Information and Development Studies (CIDES) said.
Its biggest election win so far was 73.17 of the votes in 1987.
